name.text: L1 — Dialogue 1: location of the crack

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Where is the crack that Jānis reports?

generalfeedback.text: Jānis reports the crack "on the leading edge of a turbine blade" — the front edge that meets the airflow first.

feedback.text: Correct — stage-one turbine blade, on the leading edge near the tip.
No — that is where the visual findings are, in Dialogue 3.
No — the corrosion is near the fastener holes, not the crack.

name.text: L2 — Dialogue 1: severity of the crack

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Jānis says the crack looks deep.

generalfeedback.text: He says "the crack looks shallow, although the line is very clear." Shallow, not deep.

feedback.text: No — he says the crack looks shallow.
Correct — the crack looks shallow, but the line is clear.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How long is the crack, in millimetres? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: The borescope measuring tool reads the crack at about 4 mm along the edge.

feedback.text: Correct — about 4 mm.
3 mm is the serviceable limit, not the crack length.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. What is the serviceable limit for a crack on the leading edge, in millimetres? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: "The maintenance manual allows three millimetres for a crack on the leading edge." The limit is 3 mm.

feedback.text: Correct — the limit is 3 mm.
4 mm is the measured crack, which is longer than the limit.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. How deep is the fan-blade dent, in millimetres? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: "Our dent is one point five millimetres." The dent is 1.5 mm, shallower than the 2 mm limit.

feedback.text: Correct — 1.5 mm, within limits.
2 mm is the limit for the dent, not the measured depth.

name.text: L6 — Dialogue 3: decision on the scratch

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. What do they decide to do with the scratch?

generalfeedback.text: The scratch is 0.1 mm and the limit is 0.2 mm. It is shallower than the limit, so they accept it and record it.

feedback.text: Correct — it is within limits, so accept and record it.
No — that is the crack, which is out of limits.
No — blending is for the light corrosion, not the scratch.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. How deep is the scratch, in millimetres? Write the number only.

generalfeedback.text: "The scratch is zero point one millimetres, and the limit is zero point two." The scratch is 0.1 mm.

feedback.text: Correct — 0.1 mm, shallower than the 0.2 mm limit.
0.2 mm is the scratch limit, not the measured depth.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 4 (the voicemail) again. Jānis refers the crack to engineering because it is out of limits.

generalfeedback.text: "Because the crack is out of limits, I refer this finding to engineering for a decision." True.

feedback.text: Correct — the crack is longer than the limit, so he refers it.
No — he does refer the crack, because it is out of limits.

questiontext.text:
Read the task-card extract, then answer.

TASK CARD 72-31-00-210. Inspect the stage-1 turbine blades with a borescope. Record any crack, dent or erosion. A nick on the trailing edge is acceptable up to 1.5 mm. A nick that is deeper than 1.5 mm must be referred to engineering.

A technician measures a trailing-edge nick at 2 mm. This nick is:

generalfeedback.text: 2 mm is deeper than the 1.5 mm limit, so the nick is out of limits and must be referred.

feedback.text: Correct — 2 mm is deeper than the 1.5 mm limit.
No — 2 mm is above the 1.5 mm limit.
The card says refer it, not blend it.

questiontext.text:
Read the service-bulletin extract, then answer.

SB A320-72-1043. Inspect the fan blades for erosion on the leading edge. A blade with erosion wider than 6 mm is out of limits and must be removed. A blade within the limit may stay in service.

A blade with 8 mm of leading-edge erosion may stay in service.

generalfeedback.text: 8 mm is wider than the 6 mm limit, so the blade is out of limits and must be removed.

feedback.text: No — 8 mm is wider than the 6 mm limit.
Correct — it is out of limits and must be removed.

questiontext.text:
Read the work-order extract, then answer.

WORK ORDER 4471 — wing access panel. Light corrosion was found near the lower fastener holes. Procedure: blend light corrosion, then apply primer. Refer any corrosion with deep pitting to engineering.

What must the technician do with corrosion that has deep pitting?

generalfeedback.text: Light corrosion is blended; corrosion with deep pitting is out of limits, so it is referred to engineering.

feedback.text: Correct — deep pitting is out of limits.
That is the action for light corrosion, not deep pitting.

answer.text: Accept it and close the order.

feedback.text: No — you never accept an out-of-limits finding.

questiontext.text:
Read the MEL extract, then answer.

MINIMUM EQUIPMENT LIST. One of the two windshield heat systems may be inoperative for up to three days, provided the other system works normally. The aircraft may then be dispatched.

With one windshield heat system inoperative and the other working, the aircraft may be dispatched for up to three days.

generalfeedback.text: The MEL allows dispatch with one system inoperative for up to three days, if the other works. True.

feedback.text: Correct — dispatch is allowed for up to three days under the MEL.
No — the MEL does allow it, if the other system works.

questiontext.text:
Read the built-in-test readout, then answer.

BITE READOUT — WEATHER RADAR. Fault 34-11, antenna drive. The test shows the fault is present now (a hard fault), not intermittent. A hard fault must be rectified before dispatch.

According to the readout, a hard fault must be:

generalfeedback.text: The readout states a hard fault is present now and must be rectified before dispatch — not merely logged or deferred.

feedback.text: Correct — a hard fault must be rectified before dispatch.
Recording alone is not enough for a hard fault.

answer.text: Left until the next scheduled check.

feedback.text: No — a hard fault cannot be deferred to the next check.

questiontext.text:
The crack is 4 mm. The limit is 3 mm. Complete with one word:

"The crack is ______ than the limit." (long)

generalfeedback.text: Short adjective: add -er. long → longer. 4 mm is longer than 3 mm, so the crack is out of limits.

feedback.text: Correct — longer than the limit.

questiontext.text:
Complete with one word:

"The pit is ______ than allowed." (deep)

generalfeedback.text: Short adjective: deep → deeper. Note "than", not "then" or "as".

feedback.text: Correct — deeper than allowed.

name.text: U3 — correct the error: more small

questiontext.text:
This sentence has a comparative error: "The dent is more small than the limit."

Write the correct comparative word for "small".

generalfeedback.text: Never use "more" with a short adjective. small → smaller, not "more small".

feedback.text: Correct — smaller.

questiontext.text:
Complete with one word:

"The scratch is shallower ______ the limit."

generalfeedback.text: A comparison uses than — not "as", "from" or "then".

feedback.text: Correct — "than" links the comparison.

questiontext.text:
Complete with two words:

"This finding is ______ ______ than the last one." (severe)

generalfeedback.text: Long adjective: use more. severe → more severe, never "severer".

feedback.text: Correct — more severe than.

name.text: U6 — bank term: the allowed maximum

questiontext.text:
Complete with the bank term (two words):

"The largest damage the manual allows is the ______ ______."

generalfeedback.text: The serviceable limit is the largest damage the manual allows for a part to stay in use.

feedback.text: Correct — the serviceable limit.

name.text: U7 — bank term: bigger than allowed

questiontext.text:
Complete with the bank term (three words):

"A crack that is bigger than the manual allows is ______ ______ ______."

generalfeedback.text: Bigger than the limit = out of limits — the part is not serviceable.

feedback.text: Correct — out of limits.

questiontext.text:
Complete with one word:

"The crack is ______ than the manual allows." (big)

generalfeedback.text: Short vowel + consonant: double the last letter. big → bigger, never "more big".

feedback.text: Correct — bigger.

name.text: V1 — match the defect to its meaning

questiontext.text: Match each defect to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: borescope = a camera on a probe; corrosion = metal breaking down; pitting = small holes; dent = a pushed-in hollow; erosion = material worn away.

answer.text: a camera on a probe that looks inside an engine
metal that breaks down by reacting with air or water
small holes or pits in a surface
a small hollow where a surface is pushed in
material worn away by hot gas or particles

name.text: V2 — match the term to its action

questiontext.text: Match each term to the action or meaning that fits it.

generalfeedback.text: serviceable limit = check it in the manual; blend = smooth a small defect; accept = leave it in service; repair = make it serviceable again; refer = pass it to engineering.

answer.text: the largest damage the manual allows
smooth away a small defect within limits
leave the part in service as it is
fix the part so it is serviceable again
pass the finding to engineering for a decision

questiontext.text: Which term means the front edge of a blade that meets the airflow first?

generalfeedback.text: The leading edge is the front edge that meets the airflow first — where the reported crack sits.

feedback.text: Correct — the front edge that meets the airflow.
No — that is the largest damage the manual allows.
No — that is a check made by looking carefully.

questiontext.text: Which collocation is correct?

generalfeedback.text: The natural verb is run (or carry out) a borescope inspection — not "close" or "blend" one.

feedback.text: Correct — run (or carry out) a borescope inspection.
No — you close a work order, not an inspection.
No — you blend a surface defect, not an inspection.
